newsitem.title: USA: New LME cleared options volume set to rise - Wolff.
newsitem.headline: New LME cleared options volume set to rise - Wolff.

text.p: Trading in the London Metal Exchange's new traded average price options, or TAPOs, is to set rise sharply and take away business from the existing over-the-counter Asian options market and the LME's current traded options, Mo Ahmadzadeh, president of Rudolf Wolff and Co Inc, said.
Since TAPOs were introduced for copper earlier this month, he said, they have traded at half a percent volatility premium over the traded options.

Ahmadzadeh said a TAPO option should theoretically be cheaper than an option based on a fixed date within a month. LME traded options are declared on the first Wednesday of the month and priced on the third.

In a briefing here during Copper Club week, Ahmadzadeh noted that the $2,000 strike price for the fourth quarter of 1997 TAPOs was trading at a 0.5 percent volatility premium over the equivalent traded option.
"People are trying to get away from over-the-counter basis -- that's the hangover from Sumitomo," Ahmadzadeh said.
Many grantors of over-the-counter Asian options had their fingers burnt when copper prices crashed following Sumitomo Corp's announcement of huge losses from alleged unauthorised copper dealings.
Ahmadzadeh said copper producers would be attracted to TAPOs because much of the red metal pricing was done on an average monthly price basis.
TAPOs were also launched for aluminum, but Ahmadzadeh said he thought that market was more interested in fixed price transactions than a product based on monthly average prices.
Ahmadzadeh said he thought market participants would be surprised at how much producer activity in the options market would be revealed by volume and open interest figures in TAPOs.
"The visibility of the depth of producer interest will give everyone a sense of much underlying activity in the market place arises from producers," Ahmadzadeh said.
